question: Which major public health issue heavily impacts teenage girls in many Nigerian communities?
explanation: Adolescents face significant vulnerabilities regarding reproductive health, making unplanned pregnancies and unsafe abortions a leading concern in clinical practice. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why must midwives look beyond biological symptoms when caring for young clients?

options.A: Social factors and poverty heavily influence health decisions
options.B: Teenagers rarely experience genuine physical illnesses
options.C: Biological symptoms are identical across all age groups
options.D: Laboratory tests are completely unavailable in local clinics

explanation: Understanding a young person's background, education, and economic status is vital because these social determinants dictate how and when they seek care. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary reason teenagers avoid visiting healthcare clinics for reproductive health services?

options.A: Lack of interest in personal hygiene
options.C: Fear of judgment and lack of privacy

explanation: Adolescents frequently stay away from clinics because they worry healthcare workers will judge their behavior or break their trust by telling others. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h2)

question: A 16-year-old girl visits the clinic for contraception and asks if her mother will find out. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Refuse to provide any counseling until she returns with an adult
options.B: Tell the teenager that healthcare secrets do not exist in hospitals
options.C: Call her mother immediately to inform her of the visit
options.D: Explain the rules of confidentiality and its legal limits clearly

explanation: Clear communication about privacy builds immediate trust while ensuring the client understands safety exceptions like abuse or self-harm. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h2)

question: What type of question is best for encouraging an adolescent to share their full story?
explanation: Open-ended questions prevent simple yes-or-no answers and prompt young clients to explain their thoughts and feelings in detail. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h3)

question: How does reflective listening help during a counseling session with a teenager?

options.A: It forces the client to agree with the prescribed treatment
options.B: It speeds up the consultation so the clinician can leave early
options.C: It proves the midwife is an expert in medical terminology
options.D: It shows the midwife understands and validates their feelings

explanation: Repeating back a summary of what the teenager said builds rapport and ensures both parties are on the same page. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why are peer education programs often successful among teenagers?

options.A: Peer educators are licensed medical doctors and surgeons
options.B: Teenagers prefer lectures delivered by elderly community leaders
options.C: Peer educators never require any training or supervision
options.D: Young people relate better to peers who share their experiences

explanation: Adolescents open up more easily to individuals close to their own age who understand their daily social pressures and language. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h4)

question: A midwife is setting up a youth club in a secondary school. What is the most important role for the midwife in this setup?

options.A: Banning students from asking questions about sexual health
options.B: Handling administrative funding and school fee collections
options.C: Taking over all conversations so students never speak to each other
options.D: Providing accurate training and ongoing supervision for peer leaders

explanation: Midwives must ensure peer educators receive correct medical facts and clinical back-up while allowing youth leaders to run the discussions. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common institutional barrier for adolescents seeking clinic care?

options.A: Availability of dedicated youth-friendly service corners
options.B: Long waiting queues alongside pregnant adult women
options.C: Judgmental attitudes from healthcare reception staff
options.D: Demands for mandatory parental consent for basic care

explanation: Youth-friendly corners actually remove barriers and encourage attendance, whereas long queues, judgmental staff, and strict consent rules drive adolescents away. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why is it important to involve religious and traditional leaders in adolescent reproductive health advocacy?

options.A: They hold significant influence over community attitudes and parental support
options.B: They manage the financial budgets of all public health clinics
options.C: They possess advanced degrees in gynecology and midwifery practice
options.D: They are legally required to sign every prescription written by midwives

explanation: Winning the support of community and religious leaders helps reduce cultural resistance and fosters acceptance of youth health programs. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating adolescent reproductive health program outcomes?

options.A: To replace all clinical workers with automated computer software
options.B: To increase the cost of medical consultations at the local facility
options.C: To punish staff members who fail to meet unrealistic patient quotas
options.D: To determine if the initiative is achieving its goals and meeting client needs

explanation: Evaluation provides the data needed to see what works well and where adjustments must be made to better serve young clients. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h6)

question: A youth outreach program has high attendance, but very few teenagers visit the clinic for services. What does this outcome suggest?

options.A: The peer educators are teaching completely accurate and flawless medical facts
options.B: All adolescents in the community are now completely free of health issues
options.C: Barriers still exist between community education and clinic utilization
options.D: The clinic has too many doctors and midwives available for consultations

explanation: A gap between outreach attendance and clinic visits shows that obstacles like fear, stigma, or poor clinic policies are still blocking care. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h6)
